fixes.explanation: That's the reason, baker. The LORD tells Moses, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.” (Exodus 4:19) Word comes that the ones who wanted him gone are gone themselves. So Moses puts his wife and sons on a donkey and heads for Egypt (Exodus 4:20). He takes the staff of God in his hand, too.

Hiding is a good guess, friend, but the text gives a different reason. The LORD says, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.” (Exodus 4:19) Nothing there about the Israelites promising anything. Then Moses puts his wife and sons on a donkey and heads back to Egypt (Exodus 4:20).

Close, baker, because Jethro is where this trip begins. Moses goes back to Jethro to ask permission, and Jethro says, “Go in peace.” (Exodus 4:18) But the meeting with Aaron happens somewhere else. Aaron “…met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.” (Exodus 4:27)

Moses doesn't keep a thing back, friend. “…Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs He had commanded him to perform.” (Exodus 4:28) That's the whole download, signs included. Then Moses and Aaron go and assemble the elders (Exodus 4:29). So Aaron isn't sitting there waiting for a big 'ta-da' at that meeting.

Not a word about asking for more, friend. The text says, “…and they believed.” (Exodus 4:31) When they heard that the LORD had attended to the Israelites and had seen their affliction, they “…bowed down and worshiped.” (Exodus 4:31) Nobody's calling for a second batch of signs. Believing and bowing down is what the text gives us.

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The passage does not say that nobody is hiding anyone or that there is no secret hideout. It simply gives a different reason for Moses to return.
The passage does not say Moses starts the trip at Jethro's home or mention a doorstep.
The passage says Moses told Aaron before they gathered the elders, but it does not say nobody else had heard a word beforehand.
The passage says the people believed and worshiped, but it does not say they had already received what they needed.
